title: Bengali Wedding Guest Outfit: What to Wear (2026 Guide)
excerpt: Bengali wedding guest outfit ideas: rich jewel-tone Anarkalis and embroidered kurta sets for the evening rituals, plus the colours to leave to the bride.
body:
For a Bengali wedding, guests usually wear a silk saree or a rich Anarkali or embroidered kurta set in jewel tones such as emerald, royal blue, magenta or purple. Leave the full red-and-white bridal look to the bride, and avoid plain white, which many Bengali families link with mourning. Most of the main rituals happen in the evening, so a little shine is welcome.

This guide is for guests flying in from the UK, US, Canada or Australia who want to look festive and respectful without owning a Banarasi saree.

*By the Bahe Kurtiz styling team, Jaipur. Every piece is stitched in our own Jaipur unit, and our block prints are printed by hand by our karigars.*

## What do guests wear to a Bengali wedding?

Traditionally, women guests wear sarees: Banarasi silk, Jamdani or a crisp tant cotton for daytime. Today, Anarkalis and embroidered kurta sets are completely normal at Bengali weddings, especially for guests who travel or are not confident draping a saree.

The wedding itself, the biye, often runs late into the evening, sometimes past midnight depending on the auspicious time. Rituals such as shubho drishti, mala badal and sindoor daan happen with the whole family gathered close, so you will be seen up close and in many photos. Choose rich fabric and a colour with depth.

A taffeta silk Anarkali catches the warm lights at a Bengali wedding beautifully. Our [sage green taffeta silk Anarkali with gota work and a sequin organza dupatta](/products/sage-green-taffeta-silk-gota-work-anarkali-suit-set-with-sequin-organza-dupatta/) ($52) has the sheen of silk without a heavy saree to manage.

## Which colours should guests avoid at a Bengali wedding?

The Bengali bride usually wears a red Banarasi saree with white shakha and red pola bangles. That red and white pairing is hers, so guests avoid looking like a second bride.

### Colours to skip

- Bridal red head to toe
- Plain white, which many families associate with mourning
- All black at the main ceremony, which some families find inauspicious

### Colours that work beautifully

Emerald, bottle green, royal blue, magenta, deep purple, mustard and wine all sit well next to the bride's red. Pastels are fine for daytime events, but for the night ceremony a deeper shade looks more festive in photos.

> **From our Jaipur studio:** Under the warm yellow lights of a wedding pandal, taffeta silk glows and gota work picks up every flash. Georgette looks softer and flows more. If the ceremony runs late and the venue is crowded, georgette is the lighter, cooler choice.

## What should you wear to each Bengali wedding function?

A Bengali wedding is not one event. Here is a simple plan by function:

| Function | Time | Outfit | Fabric | Colour |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gaye holud | Morning | Cotton kurta set or tunic | Cotton, block print | Yellow, mustard, green |
| Biye (wedding) | Evening to night | Anarkali or rich kurta set | Taffeta silk, georgette | Emerald, royal blue, magenta |
| Bou bhaat (reception) | Evening | Embellished Anarkali | Georgette, organza | Purple, wine, gold |

### Gaye holud

This is the turmeric ceremony, held in the morning at home. Turmeric paste may be shared around, so wear washable cotton in yellow or green. The [yellow embroidered cotton tunic top with a black floral yoke](/products/yellow-black-embroidered-cotton-tunic-top/) ($19) with white pants is easy, cheerful and fine if a little haldi lands on it.

### Biye

This is the main event. Go for the richest piece you are bringing. The [royal blue georgette Anarkali with handwork and a gota lace dupatta](/products/royal-blue-georgette-anarkali-suit-gota-handwork-dupatta/) ($52) is a strong choice because blue looks striking beside the bride's red.

### Bou bhaat

The reception is hosted by the groom's family. It is relaxed and glamorous at the same time, and a good moment for a jewel-tone kurta set or your second Anarkali. The [plum purple embroidered cotton suit set](/products/plum-purple-embroidered-cotton-3-piece-suit/) ($48) is comfortable for a long dinner and still dressy with gold jewellery.

## How do you style an Anarkali for a Bengali wedding?

A few small touches make a kurta set or Anarkali feel right at a Bengali wedding:

1. Gold-tone jewellery: Bengali weddings lean towards gold, so jhumkas or a choker look natural.
2. A small bindi: red or maroon, if you usually wear one.
3. A neat low bun with flowers, which keeps hair off your neck during the long evening ritual.
4. Flat embroidered juttis or block heels, since you may be standing around the mandap for a while.

This season, deep greens and blues with gold thread are a popular choice for evening wedding guests.

A final note on etiquette: Bengali weddings are warm and family-centred. Dress richly, stay respectful during the rituals, and let the bride own the red.

## Frequently asked questions

**Can I wear red to a Bengali wedding as a guest?**
A red accent or border is fine, but avoid a full red outfit that looks bridal. Jewel tones are the safer choice.

**Is it okay to wear white to a Bengali wedding?**
Plain white is best avoided, as many Bengali families associate it with mourning. White with a bold coloured border or heavy embroidery is less of a concern, but check with the host if unsure.

**Do I have to wear a saree to a Bengali wedding?**
No. Anarkalis and embroidered kurta sets are widely worn by guests today, especially by those who travel.
